rows.title: ISE: An Execution-Grounded Recipe for Multi-Turn OS-Agent Trajectories
rows.pre_filter_rationale: Directly addresses agentic systems, multi-turn trajectory data synthesis, and tool-use evaluation—core to production agent development. The execution-grounded approach (Stage 3) and ablation methodology are practically relevant for building reliable OS agents.
rows.summary: ISE is a three-stage execution-grounded synthesis paradigm for generating multi-turn OS-agent trajectories: intent construction via 4D structured sampling (Persona×Domain×Task×Complexity), multi-turn role-locked user simulation with state grounding, and live OS execution validation. Produces 23,132 trajectories with authentic failure-recovery dynamics, lifting agent performance from 19.3% to 37.7% on ClawEval.
challenge_hooks: How to synthesize representative multi-turn agent trajectories that avoid intent-first and single-turn biases present in existing datasets
Preventing role drift and state hallucination in LLM-based user simulators for interactive agent training
Grounding agent training data in real OS execution outcomes rather than simulated tool responses to capture authentic failure-recovery dynamics
Measuring and ensuring semantic diversity in large-scale structured intent pools for agent training
rows.relevance_reason: OS-agent trajectory generation is tangential to core NLP/RAG/document-focused work; while agentic systems are relevant, this focuses on GUI automation rather than LLM-driven reasoning, retrieval, or knowledge work.
rows.value_rationale: The execution-grounded synthesis methodology and structured sampling approach (Persona×Domain×Task×Complexity) could inform multi-turn agent evaluation frameworks, but the OS-automation domain and ClawEval benchmark are misaligned with document intelligence, RAG systems, and knowledge-work agents that are your primary focus areas.

rows.title: Keep Policy Gradient in Charge: Sibling-Guided Credit Distillation for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agents
rows.pre_filter_rationale: Directly addresses credit assignment in long-horizon agentic RL with tool use—a production pain point—proposing a practical distillation technique (SGCD) that avoids pitfalls of naive self-distillation and demonstrates gains on standard benchmarks; relevant to building reliable multi-step agent systems.
rows.summary: SGCD addresses zero-tool collapse in long-horizon agent RL by using sibling-guided credit distillation instead of competing distillation losses. Divergence-driven credit weighting reshapes GRPO advantages while keeping policy gradient dominant, avoiding teacher-student misalignment that destroys tool-use behavior.
challenge_hooks: How to prevent self-distillation from degrading tool-use behavior in long-horizon RL agents
How to assign dense token-level credit signals without competing with outcome verification
How to leverage sibling rollout contrasts for credit reassignment in group-relative policy gradient methods
How to use privileged training-time information without creating deployment distribution mismatch
rows.relevance_reason: While addressing agent tool-use and credit assignment in RL, the paper focuses on reinforcement learning optimization rather than production agentic system architecture, retrieval integration, or deployment concerns central to applied work.
rows.value_rationale: Potentially useful if building RL-based agents with long-horizon planning, but most production agentic systems (LangGraph, multi-turn orchestration) rely on LLM reasoning and tool-use patterns rather than policy gradient methods; the techniques are research-stage RL optimization without demonstrated production deployment patterns.

rows.summary: Proposes HCPD, a zero-source hallucination detection framework that emulates human evaluators by adaptively decomposing judgments into weighted interpretable criteria, using reward-based alignment training with weak supervision and multi-sampling aggregation for robust, explainable detection without model internals or external references.

rows.value_rationale: The interpretable criteria decomposition and weak-supervision training method is actionable for building reliable LLM-as-judge evaluators in production pipelines. The zero-source design fits well into RAG systems where factuality checking against retrieved context is essential, reducing dependency on specialized models or APIs.

rows.title: Attention-Discounted Adaptive Sampler for Masked Diffusion Language Models
rows.pre_filter_rationale: Directly addresses production inference efficiency for LLMs through a training-free, modular reranking technique that improves parallel decoding quality with measurable speedup—actionable for optimizing LLM serving latency in constrained environments.
rows.summary: Introduces ADAS, a training-free attention-discounted reranking method for parallel masked diffusion language model decoding. Uses soft attention penalties to discount candidates attending to uncertain already-selected positions, improving subset construction while preserving existing samplers' stopping rules. Achieves 9-10% improvement on reasoning/code benchmarks with 3.1% overhead.
challenge_hooks: How to safely unmask multiple token positions simultaneously when their predictions are coupled and token-wise confidence alone is insufficient
Reducing joint dependence error in parallel decoding without retraining decoders or adding expensive planning/search procedures
Incorporating dependency-aware ranking into existing samplers (Top-k, entropy-budget, confidence-threshold) without redesigning stopping rules
rows.relevance_reason: Masked diffusion language models are niche architectures with limited production adoption; the reranking improvement is theoretically interesting but not actionable for mainstream LLM inference workflows.
rows.value_rationale: Relevant only if actively working with masked diffusion models (e.g., Genie, Muse-variants), which are rare in production RAG/agentic systems. The attention-discounting technique could inform custom reranking logic, but the 3.1% overhead and training-free constraint limit practical applicability compared to established inference optimization strategies.

rows.title: Optimal Post-Training Quantization Scales and Where to Find Them
rows.pre_filter_rationale: Directly applicable to production LLM deployment; PTQ is a standard compression technique for inference, and data-driven scale optimization addresses a practical bottleneck in quantization pipelines with demonstrated improvements on widely-used models.
rows.summary: PiSO algorithm computes optimal quantization scales for post-training quantization of LLMs by partitioning scale search space into intervals with closed-form minimizers. Extends to group-wise quantization and integrates with error correction methods like GPTQ, showing consistent perplexity improvements on Llama/Qwen models.
challenge_hooks: How to compute optimal quantization scales efficiently without exhaustive grid search or data-free heuristics?
How to interleave scale optimization with error correction methods to jointly refine quantization parameters and weight assignments?
How to extend optimal scale selection from channel-wise to group-wise quantization while capturing cross-group activation interactions?
How to reduce calibration data requirements while improving quantization quality at extreme bit-widths (2-4 bits)?
rows.relevance_reason: Post-training quantization is directly relevant to LLM inference optimization for production systems, though the contribution is algorithmic rather than addressing architectural or systems-level production concerns.
rows.value_rationale: PiSO provides a practical quantization tuning method that could reduce model serving costs and latency in deployed RAG/agent systems; the integration with GPTQ and empirical validation on standard models makes it actionable for inference optimization decisions within a 6-month horizon.

rows.summary: DCPM: A dual-process cognitive memory architecture for LLM agents that organizes memory hierarchically from raw inputs through atomic facts, belief trajectories, and identity to cross-domain schemas and intentions. System 1 synchronously records belief revisions as doubly-linked supersedes chains; System 2 asynchronously induces schemas and detects cross-domain behavioral patterns.

rows.value_rationale: Provides empirical benchmarking data on format robustness and representation effects for table understanding, which informs architectural decisions on how to represent tables in RAG systems and document extraction pipelines. Useful for evaluating whether to normalize table formats or use multimodal approaches in production systems.

Across diverse tasks, we find that reasoning typically crosses a \emph{commitment boundary} -- a sharp transition from transient intermediate guesses to a stable, high-confidence answer. MemRefine: LLM-Guided Compression for Long-Term Agent Memory

Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly expected to operate over long-term interactions, where information from past dialogues must be preserved and recalled to support future tasks. INFUSER: Influence-Guided Self-Evolution Improves Reasoning
